title: Dimension of products of subspaces in a field with a rational residue valuation
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $R\subset K$ be a subring containing $k$, with fraction field $K$ (every element of $K$ is a quotient of two elements of $R$). Assume $R$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and that the quotient map induces an isomorphism $k\xrightarrow{\sim}R/\mathfrak m$. Let $V,W\subset K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional $k$-linear subspaces [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] of dimensions $r,s$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Define $P$ to be the $k$-linear span of the products $vw$ with $v\in V,w\in W$, that is, the subspace of finite $k$-linear combinations of those products. Then $P$ is finite-dimensional and
$$\dim_k P\geq r+s-1.$$

source.place: Section 2.4, Theorem 5, printed p.10, the Clifford-line bound: agent auxiliary product-subspace lemma for reconstructing that bound by multiplication of sections and orders at a rational point. This auxiliary is not separately stated in Morrison. Its full valuation argument is given in the delivery report; local Morrison PDF WANTED, read online.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-rational-residue-distinct-order-basis] for $U=V$ and $U=W$. All its hypotheses are exactly those of the item. Obtain bases $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ and $w_1,\ldots,w_s$ whose orders $a_i=\nu(v_i)$ and $b_j=\nu(w_j)$ are strictly increasing. Since $V,W$ are nonzero, $r,s\geq1$.

source.place: Agent product-subspace argument using Tag 00IE (algebra-definition-value-group), the DVR normalized valuation, and the distinct-order basis auxiliary.

proof.text: Every product $vw$ is a linear combination of the $rs$ products $v_iw_j$: if $v=\sum_i c_i v_i$ and $w=\sum_j d_jw_j$, then $vw=\sum_{i,j}c_i d_jv_iw_j$. Conversely these $rs$ products belong to $P$. Thus they span $P$, which is finite-dimensional by [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace].

source.place: Agent product-subspace argument using Tag 00IE (algebra-definition-value-group), the DVR normalized valuation, and the distinct-order basis auxiliary.

proof.text: Consider the $r+s-1$ nonzero elements $v_1w_1,v_2w_1,\ldots,v_rw_1,v_rw_2,\ldots,v_rw_s$ of $P$. Multiplicativity from [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-arithmetic] gives their orders $a_1+b_1<\cdots<a_r+b_1<a_r+b_2<\cdots<a_r+b_s$. If $r=1$ or $s=1$, the corresponding segment is empty; the count and inequalities still hold.

source.place: Agent product-subspace argument using Tag 00IE (algebra-definition-value-group), the DVR normalized valuation, and the distinct-order basis auxiliary.

proof.text: Any finite family of nonzero elements with distinct orders is $k$-linearly independent here. Indeed, $c\in k^\times$ is a unit of $R$ (its inverse lies in $k\subset R$), so $\nu(c)=0$ by the value-group description in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. In a nontrivial relation, retain only terms with nonzero coefficients and order them by increasing valuation. Their weighted terms still have distinct orders by multiplicativity. Repeatedly apply the unequal-order addition formula of [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-arithmetic], starting with the largest-order term and adding terms of decreasing order. Each partial sum is nonzero and has the least order so far, so the final sum is nonzero, a contradiction. Apply this to step 3. The resulting independent family of $r+s-1$ elements extends to a basis of the finite-dimensional space $P$; hence the basis-cardinality definition [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] gives $\dim_kP\geq r+s-1$.
